- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.75) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.33) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag the true price by 1–3 days in the early part of the 30-day horizon — especially after sharp spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overcorrects and forecasts a sharp drop, but true price usually rebounds modestly or stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high prices longer than observed, especially when sentiment is neutral or declining.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.75 and 0.00), model overfits short-term noise and fails to smooth out the true trend.
- Horizon-specific: Day 1–3 forecasts are often too optimistic; Day 25–30 are too pessimistic — model underweights late-period mean reversion.
